name: entry_filter_m4_v0
status: registered before any outcome of the corpus was read
question: Using only what is known at the moment an armed setup on NIFTY or BANKNIFTY reaches its level, can a small model rank the desk's fired setups so that the setups it keeps have a higher mean outcome on the index (stop, target or 45-minute mark, in multiples of planned risk) than keeping every first-fire setup, on sessions it has never seen?

decision.may_change: if it ever applies: only skip a setup the desk would otherwise take. It can never add a setup, raise a size, loosen a gate, change a stop or target, or touch the paper-mode switch.

relation: First study on the shadow lab's corpus (quantdesk/intraday/shadowlab.py, PR #155, merged as 4f525e5). It does not repeat any registered spec: intraday_direction_v1 asked whether direction could be predicted and failed; this asks whether the desk's own armed setups can be ranked, a different target, unit and population. Overlap, disclosed and not a repeat: the same minute data was scored for direction (intraday_direction_v1, 2019 to Feb 2023) and for HAR volatility (har_oneshot_v1, 2023-03-01 to 2026-05-14, a volatility result that was read); the locked-test window and the part of validation from 2023-03-01 fall inside the second window, while the train window (its 2019 to 2022 part) and the first two months of validation (2023-01 and 2023-02) fall inside the first; the target differs from both.
not_for: Index minutes are third-party and `external_unverified`; the replay prices options on a model chain, so the label is the index outcome and carries no cost. Nothing here is evidence for a gate, the paper gate, a promotion, a DTE change, an option strategy or a profitability claim. A pass only authorises the same study on recorded real quotes with costs (T2) and a forward shadow read; it can never change the desk.

corpus.generator: python -m quantdesk intraday shadow-replay --dataset <ml-intake-2-feae259bdba6> --sample 800 --seed 20261101 --from 2016-01-01 --to 2026-05-14 --symbols NIFTY,BANKNIFTY --jobs 3 --out <new folder outside every git tree>
corpus.code: run from main at or after 4f525e5 (the merged shadow lab). The manifest RECORDS the commit, whether the tree is dirty and the dataset digest; the code does not refuse on any of them. Before the read the analyst checks that the commit is on main, the tree is clean and the digest equals the one below, and writes the three checks into the run log; a failed check voids the run.
corpus.sessions: 800 drawn at random without replacement from the sessions after the first 250 (the engine's lookback), 2016-01 to 2026-05-14, seed fixed above; about 2,530 sessions are eligible. The dataset's default set is used: its review sessions (for example 2020-03-13) and its special sessions (Muhurat, Saturday) are not in it (see limitations).
corpus.unit: an idea: the first LABELLED fire of a setup on a symbol and direction (`idea_first`); later re-arms within 45 minutes are the same idea. The corpus generator drops a fire with no usable outcome before it marks ideas, so when a first fire is dropped the next labelled re-arm inside the 45 minutes becomes the idea; this is the same for every arm and does not depend on any model. Training, validation and test rows are `idea_first` rows only. The evaluation unit is the session, because ideas of one day share the market.
corpus.engine: the desk's engine as merged, empty learning memory per session (no research priors, warehouse flows or buyer edge: the naive engine), model option chain priced on the dataset's own INDIAVIX minutes where the dataset has them for the day (point in time), else the engine's constant 14.0 vol fallback; adverse ticks 1. The dataset's VIX is itself unverified. The fallback sessions are about 1 to 2% of sessions by the dataset's own coverage table; they stay in, their number is reported, and a re-score without them (identified from the dataset's VIX coverage, not from the engine's output) is reported and decides nothing.
corpus.expected_size: about 3.7 ideas per session from a 100-session probe (counts only), so about 3,000 ideas, about 540 in the locked test. The probe ran on the engine BEFORE the VIX correction (constant 14.0), so the figure is approximate for the corrected engine; it is a planning number, not a rule input.

target.definition: r_underlying: after the fill, the first of: the stop (invalidation) touched = -1; the target = fill +- max(reward_risk x risk, min_move) touched = +reward/risk; otherwise the last usable (non-missing) close inside the 45-minute window, which is the 45th minute's close when that bar has one, marked in multiples of planned risk. A bar whose close is missing is not read at all, for the stop and target as well as for the exit. The stop wins when one bar touches both. Only bars from the minute after the firing bar are read. The win side is not bounded above by construction (a small planned risk with a min_move floor gives a large multiple), so a capped version is also reported and gates PASS (see decision_rules).
target.costs: none: this is an index outcome, not an option P&L

baseline.name: keep every first-fire setup that has a usable outcome (what the desk's setup logic produces before any filter; a fire whose plan is not valid, or with no bar carrying a usable close inside its 45-minute window, is dropped by the label generator and is in no population)
baseline.metric: mean r_underlying over the locked test's ideas
baseline.decision_rule: the model must beat it as set out under decision_rules; also reported, not decisive: the desk's own gate on the model chain (`desk_taken`), a random keep of the same size by idea, and the setup-cell benchmark below

benchmark_cell.name: setup x symbol cell mean
benchmark_cell.rule: score = the train-window mean r_underlying of the idea's (setup, symbol) cell (a cell with no train idea scores the train-window mean of all ideas); keep by the same frozen-threshold rule as the model (threshold from the validation scores), same q as the frozen pair
benchmark_cell.reading: reported beside the model, decides nothing. `Beat` means the model's locked-test delta (point estimate) is larger than the cell rule's delta; no interval is claimed for the difference. If the model passes but does not beat this cell rule on the locked test, the pass is read as setup composition (R differs mechanically by setup and reward_risk, and the stop-wins-tie rule biases it), and the cheaper cell rule, not the model, is what the follow-up study carries.

features: risk_pct (planned risk as % of the fill)
view_iv (the model chain's ATM implied vol from the minute's India VIX)
view_chg (the index's change on the day so far)
data.known_at: every feature is a field of the analyst's view or the armed setup at the minute of the fire; none reads a later bar. Checked by reading the replay code (not a result): bars are masked to closed minutes at the fire and the label reads only bars from the fire on.
data.encoding: categorical fields (setup, symbol, direction, kind, view_bias, view_day_type, view_vol_view, view_phase, weekday): one-hot over the levels seen in the train window, a level unseen in train is all zeros. Numeric fields: a missing value (None) is replaced by the train-window median plus a missing-indicator column for M1; M2 takes it as NaN. The scaler and the medians are fitted on the train window only. There is no refit on train plus validation before the test: the model is frozen as fitted on train.
excluded: every `desk_*` column (the desk's own decision and model-chain P&L)
r_underlying, exit_reason, exit_ts, mfe_r, mae_r, target, bars_after (the label and what follows the fire)
view_vwap, fill, level, invalidation (price levels, non-stationary)
chain_source, adverse_ticks, chain_age_min, tape_ok, bar_gap (replay and data-quality bookkeeping)
index_frozen, data_clean (computed over the whole day's bars, so they use information from after the fire: descriptive subsets only, never features)
data.audit: an allow-list: the table the models see has exactly the columns of `features` above (after encoding) and no other; any other column, including a new one the lab adds later, fails the audit. This replaces a list of what is absent.

split.rule: by session date; one session is dropped on each side of a boundary; the model, the keep threshold and every setting are frozen at the cutoff; the locked test is read once. No embargo is added beyond the purge: a label lasts at most 45 minutes inside one session and every feature looks backward, so no label or feature crosses a session boundary.
split.pinned_code: the study pipeline (features, encoding, both models, the selection, the canary, the audit, the bootstrap and the permutation) is written and tested on a SYNTHETIC table only and committed to main before the corpus is generated; its commit sha is recorded in an amendment entry of this spec, in a commit to the PR, before any validation or test label is read. No part of it is debugged on validation or test labels; a defect found after that point is a VOID with an amendment that repairs the code only. The corpus files' SHA-256 are recorded in the same commit-to-the-PR step, after generation and before any label is read.
split.freeze: before any locked-test label is scored, the frozen pair (model, C where it applies, q), the model's fitted parameters, the keep threshold and the feature list are written to a freeze file; its SHA-256 is written to the run log AND committed to the PR (an amendment entry) before the test read, so the anchor sits outside the analyst's machine. No such function exists at registration: it is written with the analysis code and its tests before any locked-test label is scored, and the locked-test labels are read only through it. It refuses to run unless every pre-read control has passed and its result is recorded in the run log, and that hash exists and matches the file. This is what `read once` means: the labels exist in the corpus file from the day it is generated, so the guard is the code path, the recorded control passes and the recorded hash, not their absence. A digest of the control results is committed with the freeze hash in the same amendment entry, and each VOID re-run commits its own freeze hash.

model.family: two small CPU models, both trained on the train window only

settings.M1: L2 logistic regression on win = (r_underlying > 0), standardised numeric features, C in {0.1, 1, 10} chosen on the validation window by log loss (an inner choice inside M1 made before any delta is looked at; it does not add pairs)
settings.M2: gradient-boosted trees (sklearn HistGradientBoostingRegressor) on r_underlying: max_depth 3, 200 iterations, learning rate 0.05, min_samples_leaf 20, early stopping off, random_state 20261105
settings.score: M1: predicted P(win); M2: predicted r
settings.keep_fraction: q in {0.3, 0.5, 0.7}: the keep threshold is the (1 - q) quantile of the model's scores on the VALIDATION window (the model out of sample, no labels used), frozen at the cutoff; an idea is kept if its score is at or above it. The realised kept fraction on the locked test is reported and must lie within q +- 0.10, else the result is MIXED unless KILL applies (the pair did not do what was frozen). It is not forced to q.

multiple_testing: 6 (model x keep fraction) pairs are scored on the validation window only; the pair with the highest validation mean R of the kept ideas is frozen; the locked test reads that one pair, so the test is a single comparison. The validation scores of all six are reported. The three C values of M1 are an inner choice by log loss, disclosed here and not counted as pairs.
controls_before_the_read: the harness's temporal checks (the ml/splits.py verifier: no overlap between windows) pass on this table

label-equal injection: the allow-list audit runs on the REAL tables first and must pass; only then is a column equal to r_underlying added to the train and validation tables, as the one and only exception to that audit (the audit is not run again on the injected table, and the injected column never reaches the study's tables); the frozen pair's validation delta with it must be at least +0.10 R, else the harness is blind to a leak and the study is VOID

selection-bias and harness check (the label-shuffle canary): 200 permutations of the TRAIN-window labels (seed 20261102); on each, the model of the FROZEN pair (model, C, q held, no re-selection) is refitted on the shuffled train labels, its keep threshold is taken from its validation scores as in the study, and delta (kept minus all) is scored on the real VALIDATION labels. With the pair held there is nothing to select, so a clean pipeline's 200 deltas are centred on zero. The control passes if the absolute mean of the 200 deltas is at most 2 standard errors of that mean (the standard error is the sample sd of the 200 deltas divided by the square root of 200). The 95th percentile of the 200 deltas is recorded and compared with the real validation delta of the frozen pair, as information only; the PASS delta plays no part in this control. This check finds selection bias and harness faults; it cannot find a feature that encodes the outcome (shuffled train labels give such a feature nothing to exploit), so the leak claim is carried by the allow-list audit and by the label-equal injection control above, which must SEE a feature equal to the label (validation delta at or above +0.10 R) or the harness is blind and the study is VOID (the label-equal injection control above). The within-session shuffle (labels permuted inside each session, same 200 draws) is also run and reported; it decides nothing, because a day-level feature can legitimately move a shuffle that preserves session means
feature audit: the allow-list above, asserted in code, and no feature has a later timestamp than the fire
time order: max(train day) < min(validation day) < min(test day) with the purge, asserted
determinism: running the whole pipeline twice gives the same frozen pair and the same SHA-256 of the freeze file and of the six-row validation score table
corpus checks: the three run-log checks under corpus.code (commit on main, tree clean, digest equal)

decision_rules.primary: on the locked test, delta = mean r_underlying of the kept ideas minus the mean of all ideas, for the frozen (model, q)
decision_rules.uncertainty: block bootstrap over sessions (resamples below, seed fixed) for the confidence bound; and a session-block permutation test: in each of 10,000 draws, whole sessions are taken in a random order until the running idea count first reaches the model's kept count (the last session is kept whole, so a draw may exceed the count slightly), and the mean r_underlying of the drawn ideas is the null statistic; p = (1 + the number of null statistics at or above the observed kept mean) / (1 + 10,000). An idea-level permutation is anti-conservative for a model whose features are day-level, so it is only reported
decision_rules.PASS: delta >= +0.10 R, and the one-sided 95% lower bound of delta > 0, and kept ideas >= 150, and session-block permutation p < 0.05, and the realised kept fraction within q +- 0.10, and the capped delta (r_underlying capped at +3 R) > 0
decision_rules.VOID: any control above fails: the locked test is NOT read and nothing is scored. Validation outcomes have been seen by then (by the pair selection and the canary) but no locked-test outcome has, so the spec is not spent. The defect is fixed and recorded as an amendment before any locked-test read. An amendment after a VOID may repair the code or the harness only: it may not change the question, the features, the windows, the target, the model grid, q, the PASS or KILL numbers, any threshold or count in controls_before_the_read or canary, or any rule in this block. At most two re-runs after a first VOID are allowed (three attempts in all); a third VOID retires the idea for this corpus
decision_rules.KILL: after the read: delta < +0.05 R, whatever else holds (KILL takes precedence over a fraction-band MIXED). The idea is retired for this corpus and this window; a new corpus needs a new spec
decision_rules.MIXED: anything else after the read (including a realised fraction out of band, or numbers that pass but fail the capped delta): no apply, no claim; a new locked window needs a new spec (this one stays spent)

evidence.cost_stress_note: applies to the follow-up on recorded quotes only; this study's label carries no cost, so the number is vacuous here

power: about 145 test sessions and 540 ideas (expected). The standard deviation of 1.1 R per idea is an ASSUMED prior (not measured on this corpus or its probe). Ideas of one session are correlated (NIFTY and BANKNIFTY on the same day, near-duplicate setups in one direction, and day-level features that keep or drop a whole session): with an intra-session correlation of 0.3 to 0.5 the standard error of delta at q = 0.5 is about 0.065 to 0.075 R, not 0.05. The lower-bound rule then binds (delta must exceed about 0.115 R). Estimated pass probability at q = 0.5: about 7 in 10 at a true 0.15 R, about 4 in 10 at a true 0.10 R; a smaller effect is not claimed to be detectable. At q = 0.3 the standard error is about 0.07 R even with independent ideas, and the expected kept count is about 162 against the floor of 150, so size alone fails the rule in roughly a quarter of draws (kept ideas are not forced to q). The realised-fraction band (q +- 0.10) is a further way to end MIXED that these figures do not price: day-level features and two years of drift can move the realised fraction on their own. These are design-effect estimates, not measurements, and the study can fail for lack of power.

kill.rule: the locked-test delta (kept minus all) is below +0.05 R in multiples of planned risk

secondary_descriptive: delta by year and by symbol

robustness of the primary: delta on r_underlying capped at +3 R (gates PASS), the win-rate delta, the median of the kept minus the median of all, and the share of delta that comes from the top 1% of ideas by r_underlying
the realised kept fraction, and the six validation scores
the setup-cell benchmark above, the idea-level random keep and the idea-level permutation test
the re-score without the VIX-fallback sessions
transfer to stocks: the frozen model applied to the stock corpus (`--stocks`, a few sessions of liquid F&O stocks, kept out of every selection), reported with its session bootstrap and its size
the recorded-quote subset (T2, real bid and ask with the desk's slippage and a 2x slippage stress) and the `data_clean` subset, where they exist; neither decides anything
use_if_passed: only a reason to run the same ranking on the recorded real-quote tape with the desk's costs and a 2x slippage stress, and then in forward shadow for at least 40 sessions graded against the keep-all baseline, with a demotion rule (a rolling 20-session delta below zero demotes it). Applying it to the desk is a separate, reviewed, tighten-only change that the owner switches on. A failure, a mixed result or a kill is final for this corpus and this window.
limitations: the label is the index outcome, not option P&L after costs; a ranking that works on the index can still lose money in options
the minutes are third-party and unverified; a source defect could be scored as model error or as skill

tail censoring: the dataset's default set leaves out its review sessions (for example 2020-03-13) and its Muhurat and Saturday special sessions, which are among the most extreme days. A setup study depends on extreme days, so a result here holds for the default set only and says nothing about the excluded sessions; admitting them would need a new spec
setups of one session are not independent; the bootstrap and the permutation are by session

the replay engine starts each session with an empty learning memory (the naive desk); the live desk differs. Its option chain is priced on the dataset's VIX where present, else a constant 14.0 (the fallback sessions are reported)
R is not bounded above; heavy tails make a mean-based rule fragile, which is why the capped delta gates PASS and the robust figures are reported
random sampling of 800 of about 2,530 eligible sessions
amendments: 490af63 (before any outcome was read): the engine is priced on the dataset's INDIAVIX, not a constant; view_iv and view_rv moved from excluded to features

this revision (before any outcome was read, after the research review of 490af63 found the spec NOT CLEAR; the re-review of 34968f5 was NOT CLEAR on the canary, VOID edges and pinning, which the next amendment entry addresses): corrected the statement that the run is refused when dirty; reconciled the engine and VIX statements; added the tail-censoring limitation; replaced the canary and made a control failure VOID instead of KILL; restated the power with intra-session correlation; made the keep rule use the validation scores and report the realised fraction; session-block permutation; capped-R gate and robust figures; encoding, scaler, no-refit and the freeze hash; the allow-list audit and the missing excluded columns; numeric fields for every number; the setup-cell benchmark; the probe-overlap disclosure

second revision (before any outcome was read, after the re-review of 34968f5): the canary rewritten as a selection-bias and harness check with the pair held and its null measured from its own 200 draws, the leak claim assigned to the allow-list audit and the injected-leak test; VOID wording (no locked-test outcome seen), a bar on threshold changes by amendment and a cap of two re-runs, KILL precedence over the fraction-band MIXED; pinned analysis code, corpus hashes and an external anchor for the freeze hash; M2 seed and hyperparameters as numbers, the permutation stopping rule and p with a +1 correction, the unseen-cell fallback, the meaning of beat; the fraction band named as a further MIXED route in the power paragraph

wording corrections (before any outcome was read; a bot review of 97cd0db found them, each checked against the code and the dates): the overlap disclosure now separates the direction study's window from the HAR window (the first two months of validation fall in the first, not the second), and view_vol_view, a string field (rich / cheap / fair / unknown), is listed with the categorical fields

audit order (before any outcome was read; a bot review of 0dc6d0f): the label-equal injection control states that the allow-list audit runs on the real tables first and that the injected column is its one exception

guard and missing bars (before any outcome was read; a bot review of e292e9a, each checked against quantdesk/intraday/shadowlab.py): the locked-test read guard now also requires every pre-read control to have passed and be recorded in the run log, so a freeze file alone cannot open the read; the target and baseline now state what label_fire does with a fire that has no usable close in its window (dropped) and with a missing 45th-minute close (the last usable close is used), which was the behaviour all along and changes no number; and, after a further bot review of 06856b1 and the research review, the idea unit is stated as the first labelled fire, the locked-test reader is stated as an implementation requirement that does not yet exist, and the control digest and per-re-run freeze hash are committed to the PR
disclosure: At registration, only counts of rows and ideas per session and symbol had been seen from the shadow lab's runs; no value of r_underlying, exit_reason, mfe_r or mae_r from the real data had been read. The 100-session probe (seed 20261031) and this corpus (seed 20261101) draw from the same pool of sessions, so about 30 probe sessions may also be in the corpus; only the idea counts of those sessions (not outcomes) were seen, and the probe's rows are not used. The probe ran on the pre-correction engine (constant 14.0 vol). The HAR one-shot result (har_oneshot_v1) was read before this spec: it is a volatility result on dates that overlap the validation and test windows, and it is not used as an input here.
